article: 注意的化学语言：乙酰胆碱与去甲肾上腺素如何向大脑发出行动指令
topic: acetylcholine and norepinephrine neuromodulation, cortical gain control, attention

sources.title: Acetylcholine contributes through muscarinic receptors to attentional modulation in V1
sources.access_note: Open access in PMC; fetched full text
key_findings: Muscarinic receptors mediate attentional modulation in macaque V1
Scopolamine (muscarinic antagonist) significantly reduced attentional modulation (P<0.001)
Mecamylamine (nicotinic antagonist) had no effect (P=0.465)
ACh application increased ROC from ~0.677 to ~0.826 in example cell
Mechanism involves local cortical circuitry and glutamatergic feedback, not simple gain multiplication

sources.title: Muscarinic and Nicotinic Contribution to Contrast Sensitivity of Macaque Area V1 Neurons
sources.access_note: Abstract only; open-access journal but full text not fetched
key_findings: Both muscarinic and nicotinic blockade reduce V1 activity via response gain model
ACh = signal enhancement, not saliency filtering

sources.title: Adaptive gain and the role of the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine system in optimal performance
sources.access_note: Abstract only; not available in PMC
key_findings: LC has phasic and tonic modes of activity
Phasic mode: low baseline + strong phasic responses = optimal task performance
Tonic mode: high baseline + weak phasic responses = disengagement, exploration
PFC (ACC/OFC) drives LC via top-down control based on task utility

sources.title: The locus coeruleus and noradrenergic modulation of cognition
sources.access_note: Abstract only; Nature Reviews subscription required
key_findings: LC is sole source of NE to neocortex
NE modulates attention, perception, and memory retrieval
Helps brain allocate attentional resources and organize adaptive behavior

sources.title: Prefrontal acetylcholine release controls cue detection on multiple timescales
key_findings: Phasic ACh transients in mPFC accompany successful cue detection
Not present in motor cortex (region-specific)
Pre-cue ACh level predicts subsequent detection success
Dual timescale: phasic (event) + tonic (sustained attention)

sources.title: Modes and models of forebrain cholinergic neuromodulation of cognition
sources.access_note: PMC ID listed (PMC2933140) but full text access not confirmed in this session
key_findings: Tonic ACh: sustained attention support
Phasic ACh: cue detection and active maintenance
M1 activation enables persistent spiking (WM)
Theta rhythm mediates between cholinergic physiology and episodic/spatial memory

sources.title: Specific Basal Forebrain-Cortical Cholinergic Circuits Coordinate Cognitive Operations
sources.access_note: PMC ID listed (PMC6214898) but full text access not confirmed in this session
key_findings: Basal forebrain cholinergic projections are highly specific, not diffuse
Different BF regions project selectively to specific cortical areas/layers
ACh can selectively modulate specific circuits, not just global broadcast

sources.title: Nicotinic α7 receptors enhance NMDA cognitive circuits in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
key_findings: α7-nAChRs enriched in glutamate synapses of dlPFC
α7 blockade markedly reduced PFC visual space representation
Low-dose α7 stimulation selectively enhanced PFC representations
Mechanism: α7 facilitates NMDA engagement during high ACh states

sources.title: Locus coeruleus-norepinephrine modulation of sensory processing and perception: A focused review
key_findings: LC-NE influences cortical and subcortical sensory neurons across modalities
Framework: adrenergic receptor expression, dose-dependent physiology, E/I balance

sources.title: Beyond traditional approaches to understanding the functional role of neuromodulators in sensory cortices
sources.access_note: Abstract only; open-access journal but full text not fetched in this session
key_findings: NE and ACh facilitate evoked responses, increase signal-to-noise ratio across multiple sensory cortices
Traditional approach gap with spike timing precision concepts
